source_text: Quod autem non fuerit aliter commiscendus Adam mulieri suae, quam eo genere quod inolevit, et forma membrorum, et Dei benedictio haud aliter in pecora quam in homines prolata, et ipsa historia testatur, quae ut ostendit formatam naturam corporum, ita non asserit immutatam. Contra quod universitatis testimonium nihil invenitur in lege Dei; nisi in Manichaei libris, qui hanc concupiscentiam a principe tenebrarum commentatur infusam.
pass_a_gloss: But that Adam was not otherwise to be mingled with his wife than by that kind which grew in, both the form of the members, and God's blessing brought forth no otherwise upon cattle than upon humans, and the history itself testifies, which as it shows the nature of bodies formed, so it does not assert it changed. Against which testimony of the universe nothing is found in the law of God; except in the books of Manichaeus, who invents this desire infused by the prince of darkness.

lemmas.lexica: LS concupiscentia=eager desire; Blaise Christian usage often sexual desire vs nuptiae
Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil
LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS lex; Blaise lex Dei / sacred Law

pass_b_english: That Adam was to unite with his wife in no other way than the practice that developed is testified by the form of the organs, by God’s blessing pronounced no differently upon animals than upon human beings (Genesis 1:22, 28), and by the history itself, which shows bodily nature formed but does not declare it altered. Nothing against this universal testimony is found in God’s law—only in Mani’s books, which invent the claim that this sexual desire was poured in by the prince of darkness (Genesis 1:22) (Genesis 1:28).

choices.why: Julian distinguishes nuptiae from concupiscentia; do not flatten to 'lust' as a nature-sin substance.
Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.
Julian's standing charge: natural evil is Manichaean. Keep the sect-name, not 'dualists'.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

bible_refs.note: From Pass B Scripture tagging; wording follows Julian's Latin, not a modern Bible.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
